g.text: After human approval, Completions Daily Rollup was rebound from gw-onprem-01 to gw-onprem-02. No
data-quality duplicates were found. The schedule remains at risk until a scheduled refresh succeeds;
verify success before re-enabling it if Power BI deactivates the schedule.
The dataset's scheduled refresh repeatedly failed because gateway gw-onprem-01 was
Repoints this dataset to gw-onprem-02. Other datasets bound to either gateway may be
affected, and in-flight refreshes will fail.
Approved — gateway rebind is the right call for a repeating failure.
No duplicate keys in well_production (10 rows scanned on (well_id, production_date))
- **Error**: The same GatewayUnavailable failure has occurred in all three consecutive scheduled
refreshes (2026-08-25, 2026-08-26, and 2026-08-27) on gw-onprem-01, so another refresh would likely
reproduce it. I propose rebinding Completions Daily Rollup to gw-onprem-02, subject to human
approval, because the failure follows the current gateway and the next scheduled failure will
deactivate the schedule. This is a wider-impact change affecting every dataset bound to the
target/current gateway; an isolated refresh is not appropriate, and the schedule cannot safely be
re-enabled because no successful refresh has occurred.
- **Note**: The buttons on the original card stay visible; a second click is refused.
Approved — gateway rebind is the right call for a repeating failure.
**Gateway rebind completed for Completions Daily Rollup**
- **Error**: Power BI: Refresh failed for 'Completions Daily Rollup' - gateway unavailable (3rd
- **Action taken**: Rebound dataset from gw-onprem-01 to gw-onprem-02.
- **Outcome**: Resolved gateway configuration issue after human approval.
The same GatewayUnavailable error occurred in three consecutive scheduled refreshes (2026-08-25
through 2026-08-27). Data quality review found 0 duplicate rows in well_production on (well_id,
production_date). The schedule was at risk: one more scheduled failure would deactivate it. No
refresh was triggered because repeating failures require gateway remediation rather than another
retry. A successful refresh should be verified before considering schedule re-enablement.
